exact_english.title: The Harbor Remembers
exact_english.text: At dawn, the whole harbor answers. The sea has not become smaller; it has become navigable. Your restoration is complete. Keep charting, revisit a favorite challenge, or let the lights watch over the water until you return.

exact_english.title: The First Skiff
exact_english.text: The oldest skiffs carried mirrors instead of cargo. A keeper turned each mirror toward a light on shore, and the next boat followed its reflection. Nothing crossed the entire ocean alone.

exact_english.title: A Place to Return
exact_english.text: Before the lamps, the harbor was a promise made in chalk on a warehouse wall: leave one mooring open for the last boat. The first restoration returns that promise to the water.

exact_english.title: What a Chart Keeps
exact_english.text: A new chart does not preserve every vessel. It preserves a route, a measurement, and the reason a keeper trusted them. The fleet can be rebuilt around knowledge that remains.

exact_english.title: The Nursery Glass
exact_english.text: Prism nurseries grow slowly enough that their first keepers used weather as a calendar. The glass bends light without deciding where it should go. That is still your work.

exact_english.title: Small Lights, Large Instruments
exact_english.text: An observatory can see far and still mistake a nearby rock for open water. Skiffs supply the close observations that make its distance useful. Size is not the same as perspective.

exact_english.title: The Joined Beam
exact_english.text: The first connected harbor lamps appeared brighter together than apart. The keepers argued about the mathematics until a child pointed out the new channel between them. The argument and the channel both remained on the chart.

exact_english.title: The Survey Bell
exact_english.text: The survey bell rings for a completed record, not for a returning keeper. Notes can wait in a dry drawer. A useful harbor should let its people sleep.

exact_english.title: A Pattern Without Hurry
exact_english.text: Constellations were named by observers who returned to the same question many nights in a row. A fast hand was never a requirement. A careful eye was welcome, and another way to point was equally good.

exact_english.title: The Night Ledger
exact_english.text: A quartermaster began recording not only arrivals, but absences. An empty chair meant someone trusted the harbor to keep working. The ledger made room for that kind of trust.

exact_english.title: The Narrow Fleet
exact_english.text: One winter, the channel could carry only a handful of vessels. The keepers stopped asking which boat was best and began asking which combination could bring everyone home.

exact_english.title: A Different Tide
exact_english.text: At the outer reefs, familiar links change their strength. A route learned at home can still be useful, but it cannot be copied without looking. The sea rewards attention to what has changed.

exact_english.title: Instructions for Morning
exact_english.text: The oldest automatic plan was a note pinned beside a lamp: if the tide reaches this mark, move the mirror. The note worked because someone had made the condition precise.

exact_english.title: Tools and Choices
exact_english.text: Some keepers enjoy placing every light themselves. Others prefer to describe a plan and watch it unfold. The craft belongs to both. Automation preserves a decision; it does not supply its purpose.

exact_english.title: The Fifth Rebuilding
exact_english.text: By the fifth rebuilding, the keeper stopped counting lost hulls and started noticing familiar routes. Learning had become visible in the speed of the harbor’s return.

exact_english.title: A Margin for Doubt
exact_english.text: The best charts leave room for notes. Forecasts carry assumptions; plans meet weather. A keeper who writes down uncertainty gives the next watch something more useful than confidence alone.

exact_english.title: Six Safe Passages
exact_english.text: No two of the six passages ask for exactly the same fleet. That difference is the final lesson of the restoration. A collection of answers can be stronger than a single rule.

exact_english.title: The Last Dark Window
exact_english.text: The last window lit was an ordinary workshop facing away from the sea. Its owner said the horizon mattered more. The keepers lit it anyway. Returning home is part of a voyage.

exact_english.title: Beyond the Dawn
exact_english.text: When the restoration ended, the harbor held a quiet celebration. There were still patterns to discover and rooms to decorate. For the first time, none of them had to be finished before the lights could rest.

exact_english.title: A Shallow Channel
exact_english.intro: Only Skiffs and Nurseries fit through this inlet. Find a useful balance before the small fleet runs out of room.

exact_english.body: For three nights the harbor kept its lanterns lit. On the fourth, a single point of light answered from beyond the reef.
Mara ordered a small fleet built from ordinary timber. The old Charts stayed in the archive: this sky would need its own bearings.
The watchkeeper left a blank line for every returning star. No one knew how many lines the book would need.
Two crews argued over a heading until they compared their observations. Each had measured a different part of the same current.
The prisms grew dim before they grew bright. Their keeper called it listening, and asked the crew to wait.
A second star appeared beside the first. Their light crossed on the water, marking a path no single lantern could reveal.
The tide wheel turned while the harbor slept. In the morning its quiet work was waiting, with no demand for thanks.
Mara wrote that the night was less empty now. She left the letter open, hoping to add another observation before dawn.
The first woven chart looked wrong. Rotated toward the sea, its loose threads matched the currents exactly.
Children named the lights after boats they remembered. The archivist recorded both the names and the disagreements.
Clouds hid the stars for a day. The crew kept working from their saved bearings; uncertainty did not erase what they had learned.
A returning watchkeeper found the instruments still turning. Her replacement had left tea, a neat log, and no list of missed duties.
The new dome did not make the stars brighter. It gave everyone a place to look at them together.
The nursery crew and the skiff crew reached the same light by different routes. Both maps earned a place on the wall.
One beacon shone steadily enough that people stopped mentioning it. The keeper counted that as success.
From the outer reef, the lights on the water looked like another harbor. For a moment the crew could imagine returning to either one.
The stars brought no treasure for the warehouses. They brought bearings, stories, and a reason to paint the boats.
On the final scheduled night, the keeper closed the public watch book. Its observations remained available to anyone who wanted to try the route.
Mara placed the seasonal map beside the first restoration chart. Neither was a deadline now. Both were invitations.
The harbor kept one lantern burning after the festival. Anyone returning late would still be able to find the pier.

exact_english.title: Build your harbor
exact_english.summary: Purchases, automation, calibration and separate fleets.
exact_english.first-light-paragraph-0: Your first Spark Skiff already earns Radiance. Buy another from the harbor fleet when its price is affordable. Five producer kinds make Radiance; each successive purchase of a kind costs more.
exact_english.first-light-paragraph-1: Buy 1 makes one purchase. Buy max spends what the fleet can currently afford. Forecasts assume the displayed fleet and conditions; a later purchase or an expiring bonus can change the result.
exact_english.fleet-growth-paragraph-0: At 25, 50, 75 and 100 of a producer, that entire tier doubles its output. At 25 Charts, cross-tier connections let early producers strengthen later ones. Compare the displayed price and added network output instead of assuming the newest kind is always best.
exact_english.fleet-growth-paragraph-1: Automatic buying unlocks at 10 Charts. Choose payback-based buying or a priority order. One saved plan slot is included; extra slots hold alternative plans and do not produce extra income by themselves. Automatic Rechart needs 100 Charts and your explicit Chart-gain and minimum-run settings.
exact_english.calibrations-paragraph-0: A calibration uses one Focus charge. Trace the constellation without a timer, undo a step, or restart. The accessible crew-help button gives the same completion and Focus effect. No reflex or speed test is required.
exact_english.heading-separate-fleets: Read the rules of each fleet
exact_english.separate-fleets-paragraph-0: Challenge dossiers have separate fleets, goals, caps and connections. Your main harbor continues working. Focus, Support and Rechart are not available inside a challenge, and challenge money does not enter your main wallet.
exact_english.separate-fleets-paragraph-1: The seasonal fleet is also separate. Main-harbor Charts and paid appearances do not increase its production. The Season screen shows its saved dates, badge goals and 30-level pass. After the scheduled end, an archived run can be resumed from that screen. This development build uses a local preview schedule, not an announced public season.

exact_english.title: Rechart without surprises
exact_english.summary: What resets, what stays, and how to decide.
exact_english.reset-preview-paragraph-0: Rechart exchanges the current main fleet for permanent Charts. The first claim becomes available at 1 billion lifetime Radiance. Preview the additional Charts and the permanent multiplier before confirming. Cancelling the preview keeps your current fleet.
exact_english.reset-preview-paragraph-1: There is no universal best reset moment. A larger claim improves your permanent multiplier, while waiting lets the existing fleet keep earning. Consider the gain and the time you want to spend rebuilding; simulated strategies are not a promise of human completion time.
exact_english.reset-loss-paragraph-0: Your main-harbor Radiance wallet is cleared and purchased main producers are removed. One free starting Spark Skiff returns. New purchases then use the stronger permanent Chart multiplier.
exact_english.reset-retention-paragraph-0: Keep lifetime Radiance, existing and newly claimed Charts, Survey Notes, stored Focus, remaining Focus time, completed Surveys and their timers, and automation settings and saved plans.
exact_english.reset-retention-paragraph-1: Keep campaign restoration, archive and calibration discoveries, dossier ownership and progress, the separate seasonal fleet and pass progress, earned appearances and your preferences. Current daily contracts and the shared daily Support record remain; Rechart does not refill their allowance. Any remaining Support effect continues for its remaining time.

exact_english.title: While you are away
exact_english.summary: Offline rates, stored timers, contracts and shared Support.
exact_english.offline-rates-paragraph-0: For one continuous absence, the first 24 hours of production earn at full rate. The next 48 hours earn at one quarter rate. Production stops after 72 hours away until you return. This limit is not restarted by a loading chunk or a second tap on the return summary.
exact_english.offline-rates-paragraph-1: Returning settles your actual fleet, purchases and expiring effects over elapsed time. The return summary reports that settlement. Saving and recovery must finish before it is treated as committed progress.
exact_english.stored-timers-paragraph-0: Focus stores one charge every 2 hours, up to 12. One charge supplies 10 minutes of a 20% production effect. Spending several charges adds time rather than multiplying the strength.
exact_english.stored-timers-paragraph-1: A Survey completes every 8 hours, up to 3 stored Surveys. Collecting each gives 10 Survey Notes. Full storage waits for you to collect or spend; it does not create a streak penalty.
exact_english.daily-contracts-paragraph-0: Three daily contract slots are retained for up to seven account days. Read each assigned goal and claim it when complete. An unclaimed slot can be rerolled once. Newly assigned goals do not count activity from before assignment.
exact_english.daily-contracts-paragraph-1: A seasonal alternative uses the same daily slot and claim receipt as its main-harbor goal. Completing both routes cannot grant the slot twice. Daily boundaries use the saved account-day offset. Changing time zone does not move that boundary, and turning the clock back does not replay an earlier day.
exact_english.shared-support-paragraph-0: Free crew briefings and optional verified rewarded ads share six slots per account day. They give the same Support token. Refusing an ad, a failed ad or no available ad does not remove the free briefing route. Unspent daily tokens do not accumulate into a larger allowance tomorrow.
exact_english.shared-support-paragraph-1: Spend a token once on a 20-minute, 25% production effect, or on an eligible offline Salvage cache. Salvage is capped by genuine recorded offline production and the displayed claim; it does not double your whole absence. The token and cache cannot be claimed twice.
exact_english.shared-support-paragraph-2: Local reminders start off. Enable them only if you want them, choose quiet hours and the reminder kinds, and turn them off at any time. Opening a reminder grants nothing. Device delivery can be delayed or denied without affecting play.

exact_english.title: Choose how to spend Notes
exact_english.summary: Separate campaign needs from optional storage and decoration.
exact_english.note-costs-paragraph-0: A new challenge dossier costs 100 Survey Notes once. An owned dossier can be replayed for free. Only one challenge fleet is active at a time; replacing or restarting it discards that active run, so read the confirmation first.
exact_english.note-costs-paragraph-1: An extra saved automation-plan slot costs 50 Survey Notes. Up to five extra slots are available after automation unlocks. A core harbor decoration also costs 50 Notes once; there are six. These slots and decorations are optional for the campaign ending.
exact_english.campaign-first-paragraph-0: Some chapter goals require particular dossiers. Check Restoration before spending Notes on an optional plan slot, decoration or another dossier. Spending those Notes first can delay access to a needed dossier and therefore delay the ending.
exact_english.campaign-first-paragraph-1: A purchased plan slot only stores another plan. A decoration changes the harbor appearance. Neither is required to increase the existing plan’s efficiency. You can finish the campaign without buying every optional collection item.
exact_english.campaign-first-paragraph-2: Play at your own pace. Balance simulations compare rules and spending choices; they do not predict how many days a person will need to learn or finish the game.

exact_english.index-summary: Local copies, cloud branches, recovery codes and deletion.
exact_english.title: Save and recover your harbor
exact_english.summary: Local copies, cloud branches, recovery codes and deletion.
exact_english.local-copies-paragraph-0: The native game saves locally. Use Export my harbor in the Logbook to copy a complete export into storage you control. Keep an older copy before replacing your current harbor. An export is game data, not an account recovery code or proof of a purchase.
exact_english.local-copies-paragraph-1: If a save is damaged, the recovery screen may offer a valid backup. Keep the damaged files or your export until you have checked the restored harbor. Do not uninstall or clear app data as a first recovery step: that can remove your local copies.
exact_english.local-copies-paragraph-2: Importing chooses one complete compatible branch. It does not combine wallets, Charts or rewards. The import flow preserves the previous local branch before replacement; verify the chosen branch and its progress before continuing.
exact_english.cloud-choice-paragraph-0: An account is optional. When an account service is configured, cloud setup asks for consent and shows an account ID and recovery code. Retain both before acknowledging the code or uploading. Credentials belong in secure account storage, never in a game export.
exact_english.cloud-choice-paragraph-1: Recovering an account does not automatically overwrite a guest harbor. Inspect real cloud branches and their revisions, then explicitly choose one. The current local branch is preserved by the import flow. Upload conflicts require reviewing the latest branch; they are not resolved by adding the two wallets together.
exact_english.heading-recovery-code: Protect the code before changing it
exact_english.recovery-code-paragraph-0: Keep the account ID and recovery code somewhere you can reach if this device is lost. Do not send them in a support message or include them in a screenshot.
exact_english.recovery-code-paragraph-1: Code rotation requires the current code. Retain the proposed replacement before submitting the change. If the response is lost, the server may already have changed the code; use the retained replacement to recover and check the account rather than discarding it.
exact_english.recovery-code-paragraph-2: If the code is lost but a valid device session remains, keep that session and export your local harbor. If there is no valid session and no code, this recovery method cannot recover the account. A local save copy may still recover your game, but it cannot prove account or paid ownership.
exact_english.logout-delete-paragraph-0: Signing out ends the requested session when the service confirms it. Forgetting credentials only on this device is an offline local action; it cannot claim to revoke a remote session. Neither action is account deletion.
exact_english.logout-delete-paragraph-1: Account deletion needs explicit confirmation and the current recovery code. Confirmed service deletion removes the active account data while leaving the current local guest game. It does not cancel an Apple or Google purchase or erase an export you saved elsewhere. Backup erasure and third-party storage depend on the final operator’s policy.

exact_english.title: Credits and licenses
exact_english.summary: How this development build was made.
exact_english.development-credit-paragraph-0: Tideglass is being created by an AI-assisted development team directed by the project owner.
exact_english.visual-credit-paragraph-0: The lighthouse, harbor, staged producers and appearance overlays were authored for Tideglass as vector geometry and native drawing code. Their reusable shapes are rendered directly by the client. The store lighthouse artwork uses the same original geometry.
exact_english.score-credit-paragraph-0: The ambient pieces and effect cues were authored for Tideglass with explicit musical phrases and mathematical synthesis. No third-party recording, sampled instrument library or reference melody was incorporated into that score. Music and effects have independent volume and mute controls.
exact_english.software-credit-paragraph-0: Tideglass uses Flutter, Dart and open-source packages. Their bundled license notices are available below.

exact_english.title: Development release notes
exact_english.development-status-paragraph-0: This local development build includes the game features below. Its version is shown at the end of this page. Optional online features depend on a configured service and may be unavailable.
exact_english.included-systems-paragraph-0: The client includes the main fleet and Rechart, offline settlement and recovery, six restoration chapters, eighteen archive entries, twelve calibrations, twelve challenge dossiers, and a separate seasonal fleet with pass progression.
exact_english.included-systems-paragraph-1: It also includes free shared-slot crew briefings, automation plans, collection appearances, reduced motion, larger text, separate audio controls, and opt-in local reminders with quiet hours. Purchases and rewarded ads appear only through their configured, verified service paths.
exact_english.current-improvements-paragraph-0: The handbook now explains reset retention, offline limits, Note spending and recovery. Long headings and confirmations wrap and scroll at larger text sizes.
exact_english.current-improvements-paragraph-1: Note-spending guidance distinguishes campaign dossiers from optional plan slots and decorations. Choosing optional purchases first can postpone a needed dossier.
exact_english.release-limits-paragraph-0: Online account recovery, verified purchases, rewarded ads and soundtrack downloads may be unavailable. The game shows their configured status; local play and free crew briefings remain available.
exact_english.release-limits-paragraph-1: Available public help pages are listed below. Opening an account deletion page does not itself delete an account.
